posts.headline: The Dow fell about 1,100 points Thursday and the S&P 500 logged its sixth straight losing day — and that drop landed right in your 401(k).
posts.source: Source: Yahoo Finance market close, Nov. 19, 2026
posts.caption:
Wall Street just had one of its worst days in weeks — and if you own an index fund or a 401(k), you own this drop.

The Dow fell about 1,100 points Thursday, roughly 2.2%, to around 49,100. The S&P 500 slid about 2% — its sixth straight losing day — and the Nasdaq dropped about 2.2% (Yahoo Finance, Nov. 19). The market's 'fear gauge,' the VIX, jumped about 16% to near 28.

Why it's your money: the S&P 500 is the backbone of most retirement accounts, so a 2% down day trims the balance millions are saving on. Even Nvidia's blowout earnings this week couldn't turn the mood — the new worry is the Fed signalling rates may go up, not down.

My take: six red days in a row is unnerving, but a 401(k) is measured in decades, not days — the headline number matters far less than the one on the day you actually retire.

Has this week's selloff changed anything about how you're investing?
